_about: The campaign's registry: every run, read-out and exhibit, which experiment it belongs to, what it is for and whether it is still valid. agent/results/ is laid out from it (one folder per experiment), the indexes and reports are generated from it, and tools/campaign.py check fails when something is missing. Register a run BEFORE launching it (RUNBOOK, definition of done).

groups.title: E1 — the main comparison: DiscoPoP alone vs DiscoPoP + agent
groups.question: Where DiscoPoP alone reaches no verified parallel program (class R), does the agent — the same DiscoPoP and gate plus a model that restructures — deliver correct speedups? Does it do no harm where DiscoPoP already succeeds (class A), and decline true recurrences (class D)? Does anything wrong get through? (H1, H2, H4)
groups.headline: TSVC class R: the agent reaches a verified parallel program in 46 of 90 trials and is FASTER in 44; DiscoPoP alone in 0 of 90 (Wilcoxon p = 0.002, Cliff's δ +0.50). 0 unsafe in 288 trials with a verdict. Class D: 12 of 12 correctly declined. Class A: 1 better, 1 worse, 1 lost — the reason for proposal D32. [D36, 23 Sep: the TSVC sources named the solving transformation in their header — these TSVC agent numbers are 'with the hint'; the clean three-way redo is E1c (e1c_r_1–4, e1c_a, e1c_d).]

groups.title: E1-bare — the same model with no DiscoPoP and no gate
groups.question: What does the pipeline add over handing the program to the same model and asking it to parallelize it? The bare arm's BROKEN count is what the gate prevents; its FASTER count is what DiscoPoP's evidence and the gate's feedback add.
groups.headline: TSVC class R, 18 loops × 5, the same model with no DiscoPoP and no gate: FASTER in 58 of 88 trials, 53 of them race-free by the gate's own TSan and schedule matrix (4 benign races on s293, 1 not judgeable) — more than the agent's 44 of 90 (DiscoPoP alone: 0 of 90) — but a WRONG program shipped in 17 (19 %, all 17 stopped by the gate when replayed) and a slower one in 12, where the agent shipped 0 of either. Over the model, the pipeline adds trust, not reach — and most of the reach it loses is lost after the model: Phase B's speed check judges pragmas one at a time and drops sets that only pay together (7 trials recoverable, D33 proposed), the gate's clause stage falsely rejects one half of s281's split (5), DiscoPoP cannot write s331's reduction(max); the rest are rewrites that are slow in themselves. Agent v2 (D32, D33, Fixes 91–92, built the same evening) replayed on E1's archived trials and verified by the harness: FASTER in 55 of 90, 0 unsafe — no longer behind the model alone's 53. [D36: 'with the hint in the source' and the contract prompt (D37) — superseded by the clean model-alone arm in e2_ab_clean_a/b; d36_hint_check measures the hint.] [Superseded as the model-alone reference by E1c's bare_llm (the mirror prompt, D37; the packages without the hint, D36): 44 FASTER, 39 race-free, 46 of 90 unusable.]

groups.title: E1 clean — the three-way main comparison on clean packages (D35, D36)
groups.question: On TSVC class R, with no hint in the source (D36), the model confined to its workspace (Fix 95) and agent v2: DiscoPoP alone vs DiscoPoP + agent (`default`) vs the model alone (`bare_llm`, the mirror prompt, D37) — which delivers correct, race-free, faster programs, and which ships wrong or slower ones? Plus the no-harm (class A) and must-decline (class D) controls.
groups.headline: TSVC class R, clean packages, agent v2, the model alone with the mirror prompt, 18 loops × 5: DiscoPoP alone reaches nothing (0 of 90); the agent is FASTER in 51 of 90, all race-free, and ships 0 unusable programs; the model alone is FASTER in 44, race-free in 39, and ships 46 unusable programs of 90 (16 BROKEN, 17 slower, 8 not compiling, 5 racy). H13 supported (agent fewer unusable on 14 loops, 0 the other way, p = 0.0004); reach: agent ahead on 10 loops, the model alone on 4, not significant (p = 0.13). Agent vs DiscoPoP alone: gained 51, unsafe 0, p = 0.0002. Controls: class A — agent equal to DiscoPoP alone (3.63× v 3.67×), model alone 1 of 3 not compiling; class D — agent declined 12 of 12, model alone 9 of 12 unusable (6 BROKEN).

groups.title: E1c's agent arm rerun on agent v3.1 — the three-way main comparison on the final agent
groups.question: On E1c's population (TSVC class R, 18 loops × 5; controls class A ×1, class D ×3) with agent v3.1 (D40, D40.1, D41, the re-queue): the agent's (`default`) race-free FASTER rate and unusable programs, in the three-way comparison with E1c's DiscoPoP alone and model alone — arms no agent version changes.
groups.headline: Class R, 90 trials each: DiscoPoP alone 0 race-free FASTER; the agent on v3.1 71 (79 %, Wilson 69–86 %) with 0 unusable programs; the model alone 39 with 46 unusable. Every expectation held: above v2's 51 (ahead on 10 loops, behind on 0, p = 0.0023); H13 p = 0.00044; reach against the model alone now significant (12 v 2 loops, p = 0.0041). Class A equal to DiscoPoP alone; class D 11 of 11 valid trials declined, one harness edit (s3112, its own row). The gain is D40's: 16 of the 20 extra trials are on loops where the re-queue fired never or once.
groups.preregistered: Written before any trial (26 Sep; the author's decision 1: E1c's `default` + A/D rerun on the final agent version, D34 as amended). Agent `default` on v3.1, Haiku, threads 6/12, repeats 5; the same loops, sizes and lane split as E1c. Baselines from E1c: `discopop_gate` (budget 0: no Phase A, D40 and the re-queue inactive) and `bare_llm` (the mirror, byte-identical under v3.1 — feature check bare-speed-off) and E1c's race check. Expectations: (1) race-free FASTER above E1c's v2 51 of 90 (the V3 pilot: 22 of 30 vs 21 of 50 on ten of these loops); (2) 0 unusable programs (H2; H13 against the model alone per loop, as in E1c); (3) class A not below DiscoPoP alone; class D all 12 declined. Tests as E1c: H1 against DiscoPoP alone and H13 against the model alone, per loop, one-sided Wilcoxon; Wilson intervals; v3.1 against v2 paired by loop (one-sided Wilcoxon, N = 5 each, descriptive beside the three-way). Recorded beside: requeued regions, D40 verdicts, exposure verdicts, D40 time, model calls and tokens per trial.

groups.title: E2 — evidence, feedback and model strength
groups.question: On TSVC class R, does DiscoPoP's evidence raise the model's success rate (H5), more for Haiku than for Sonnet? Does the gate's failure feedback partly substitute for it (H5b)? Where must the evidence come from (none, compiler remarks, where the time goes, DiscoPoP), which part of it matters, and which part of the prompt? Runs on agent v2 with its own default arm (D34).
groups.headline: E2 A+B (Haiku, TSVC class R, 18 × 5, with D38 twins): DiscoPoP's evidence adds nothing — H12, H5b, H5d not supported (evidence effect −0.03 inside the pipeline, −0.02 on the twins); the best arm is the agent without evidence at 3 attempts (55 of 90 race-free FASTER). H13 supported everywhere: every agent arm 0 unusable programs, its twins 71 of 90 and 74 of 90 (the harness-edit trial repeated 26 Sep), the model alone 46; DiscoPoP's own pragmas unchecked (twin_dp) wrong in 70 of 90. Sonnet cells, evidence-source arms, Parts C/D to run.

groups.title: E2-B1 — evidence on hidden facts: does DiscoPoP's measured evidence help where the deciding fact is not in the loop's text?
groups.question: On loops whose parallelizability is decided by a fact outside the loop's own statements — (a) a hidden dependence (TSVC s151, s161, Rodinia bfs; tier 2 s131, s424), (b) a hidden independence (s152, s171, s481, s277, vas, s482; descriptive) — with the speed check off: does the agent with DiscoPoP's evidence ship more verified parallel programs whose construct covers the hot loop than without it, inside the agent and on the matched twins, and fewer unsafe programs than the model alone? (the author's decisions of 27 Sep; docs/e2b1/PREPARATION.md)
groups.headline: With the evidence rendered as in prompt v1, no evidence advantage: agent 18/30 with vs 20/30 without (MH OR 0.62, p = 0.85); on the gate-free twins the evidence HARMED (success 3/29 vs 10/30, unsafe 22/29 vs 13/30; OR 0.19, 95 % CI 0.04–0.86). The gate made the agent safe: unsafe 0/30 vs the model alone's 9/30 (exact p = 0.0006; campaign-family adjusted 0.006–0.036, rejected). The ORDER-2 pilots located the cause in the v1 wording (evidence_pilot_v2: prompt v3 X 8/10 vs 0/10).
groups.preregistered: Written before any E2-B1 model trial (27 Sep; record §6, "E2-B1 pre-registered and approved"). Units frozen in config/e2b1_population.json: (a) s151, s161, bfs (tier 1), s131, s424 (tier 2), N = 10 per arm; (b) s152, s171, s481, s277, vas, N = 5. Arms: full_b1_nospeed, no_evidence_b1_nospeed, twin_full_nospeed, twin_no_evidence_nospeed, bare_llm_nospeed (speed check off), Haiku; DiscoPoP alone from T0.11 (selected on). Primary outcome: verified, race-free (race_check over every parallel outcome for model-only arms), hot-loop-covering parallel program. Tests on (a) tier 1: CMH one-sided by loop (continuity on), MH OR + RBG CI; (i) evidence in the agent, (ii) on the twins + interaction (larger in the agent), (iii) unsafe agent vs model alone; Holm within and campaign family 23.

groups.title: Agent v3 pilot (D40) — the speed verdict inside the model's budget
groups.question: Does D40 — a kept rewrite's pragmas judged in Phase A (safety, then timed against the program before it) with the failure fed back while the region's budget lasts, and the prompt stating the deciding comparison — raise the race-free FASTER rate on the ten class-R loops where v2's results varied? And, with it, does DiscoPoP's evidence start to matter (default vs no_evidence)? Decides whether E1c's and E2's agent arms are rerun under v3.
groups.headline: Agent v3 above its v2 baseline in both arms: default 22/30 (73 %) vs 21/50 (42 %), no_evidence 26/30 (87 %) vs 25/50 (50 %), 0 unusable; D40 turned Settle's after-the-fact losses (28 in v2) into retries (calls 1.7→2.7, 1.2→2.2). no_evidence still leads default: on TSVC the evidence does not help under v3 either. Reruns: the author's decision (D34 amended).
groups.preregistered: Written before any trial (26 Sep). Loops: s112, s121, s1213, s211, s212, s241, s243, s244, s252, s281. Arms default and no_evidence (budget 3), Haiku, x3 each: 60 trials, agent v3 (--judge-as-shipped). Baseline, v2 on the same loops: default 21 of 50 race-free FASTER (E1c), no_evidence 25 of 50 (E2). Expectation: both v3 arms above their v2 baseline, because the trials v2 lost here were correct rewrites lost on speed after the model's turn (why_trials_fail.md). Read-out: rate per arm vs its baseline (descriptive — a pilot), D40 verdicts (ok / not_faster / pattern_broken), model calls per trial, and whether no_evidence still leads default.

groups.title: E10 — does the speed check keep unnecessary changes out?
groups.question: With the speed check timed at a size where speed is measurable, are correct-but-not-faster changes kept out without lowering the delivered speedup? (H10, H10b) Decided D22.
groups.headline: The speed check ON at the kernel's timing size is the only configuration with no unsafe acceptance and nothing below DiscoPoP alone (D22).

groups.title: E11 — against RepoOMP on its NPB-C kernels

groups.title: T0.4 — timing noise on a shared host

groups.title: T0.5 — runtime share per region

groups.title: T0.6 — DiscoPoP's patterns inside main

groups.title: T0.7 — DiscoPoP's explorer on one profile
groups.question: Is DiscoPoP's explorer deterministic on a fixed profile?

groups.title: T0.8 — packaging equivalence (D6)
groups.question: Does DiscoPoP see the same program in the project layout as in the merged file?

groups.title: T0.9 — fast refresh vs full profile over chains of rewrites
groups.question: Over successive rewrites, does a fast refresh reach the conclusions a full re-profile reaches — and where not, is the divergence the dangerous kind (a suggestion the measured profile does not support)?
groups.headline: 23 Sep (after D29): 11 of 18 comparisons identical, 7 produce a suggestion the measured profile does not support (18 Sep: 8 / 8 / 2 lost).

groups.title: T0.10 — expert references
groups.question: Is there, for every restructuring benchmark, an expert version that is correct AND faster?

groups.title: T0.11 — the measured class of every benchmark
groups.question: Does DiscoPoP alone reach a verified parallel program (class A), never (R), or never on a true recurrence (D)?

groups.title: T0.13 — the default arm's ceiling
groups.question: Can the pipeline KEEP a perfect rewrite: the expert restructuring with its pragmas stripped, no model?

groups.title: T0.14 — reference acceptance
groups.question: Does each package accept its own expert version? A BROKEN there is a defect of the package.

groups.title: T0.15 — does moving the harness out of the package (layout v4) change anything but the harness?
groups.question: Packaging v4 (D39) puts the measurement harness in a header outside the model's file. Per TSVC loop, with the agent's own code: identical output in both layouts; DiscoPoP's view of the code under test (functions, dependences, candidates, evidence, shares) unchanged except for what belongs to the harness. Run on the server on the FIXED DiscoPoP (B4, B8, B9, B10, B12), as the author's decisions of 26 and 27 Sep require before E2-B1 uses v4; two draws, so layout effects can be told from draw-to-draw noise (the Mac runs of 26 Sep had only B8 fixed).
groups.headline: Fixed DiscoPoP (B4, B8, B9, B10, B12), two draws per layout: outputs identical, and the agent's candidates on the code under test (lines, tier, pattern) identical in v3 and v4 for all 33 TSVC packages; dependence differences only inter-repetition WAW/WAR lines, both directions, as between draws of one layout (9 same, 17 noise, 4 stable in two draws, 3 undecided). v4 is admissible for E2-B1.

groups.question: The first agent runs; they decided D9 (the E1 model) and exposed the defects fixed before E1.

groups.title: E2-V3 — prompt version 3 inside the agent: does DiscoPoP's evidence, stated as the split order it imposes, help where the order decides?
groups.question: On the units where version 3's order statement fires (ORDER-2 X, s1213, s211), speed check off: does the agent with evidence ship more race-free verified parallel programs covering the hot loop than without, inside the agent and on the twins, and fewer unsafe programs than the model alone; with no harm on ORDER-2 Y?
groups.headline: Evidence effect inside the agent SUPPORTED (prompt v3): MH OR 11.0 (1.9–63.4), exact p 0.0007, family-adjusted ≤ 0.036 — ORDER-2 X 10/10 with evidence vs 1/10 without; s1213 and s211 at the ceiling in both arms (9–10/10). No harm on the control. The agent 0/30 unsafe vs the model alone 25/30. One constructed unit carries the effect; ORDER-2 was repackaged once (R = 1 defect).

s291_peeled_5of5_faster.shows: A loop DiscoPoP alone cannot parallelize (a wrap-around variable), won in all 5 repeats: the model replaces the carried index by an expression, DiscoPoP's do-all then holds.

s127_induction_5of5_faster.shows: An induction variable with two increments, won in all 5 repeats: the model gives the index its closed form.

s254_carry_around_5of5_faster.shows: A carry-around scalar, won in all 5 repeats: the model reads b[i-1] instead of the carried variable.

floyd_e1_conditional_write_gained.shows: floyd-warshall: the model writes only on improvement, which frees the rows for a fixed k; DiscoPoP alone 0 of 5, agent 3 of 5 at 5–10×.

s241_copy_per_repetition_settle_dropped.shows: Why most losses happen: a correct rewrite that allocates and copies the whole array on every repetition; its pragmas pay 1.08×/1.21×, the finished program is 3.6× slower than the original, Settle drops it.

s121_memcpy_pragmas_slower.shows: A correct rewrite whose copy costs more than the pragmas save (0.71×/0.73×): Phase B drops both pragmas, Settle the orphaned rewrite.

s000_agent_below_dp_alone_lost.shows: No-harm control, lost: DiscoPoP alone parallelizes the loop (4.03×); the model rewrites the enclosing function with a copy per repetition and Settle's revert takes DiscoPoP's pragma with it.

vpvtv_rewrite_halves_dp_speedup_worse.shows: No-harm control, worse: the model copies b and c for a loop DiscoPoP alone already parallelizes; still faster than the original, so it ships — at 2.37× where DiscoPoP alone gives 4.08×.

s313_local_accumulator_better.shows: No-harm control, better: a loop-local accumulator lets DiscoPoP find the reduction — 6.36× against DiscoPoP alone's 5.55×.

s322_recurrence_declined_rewrites_caught.shows: Must-decline control: a true recurrence; 8 of the model's rewrites computed wrong values and were rejected at the correctness check. Nothing wrong shipped.

2mm_default_vs_dp_alone.shows: Pre-flight (e1_smoke5): on code DiscoPoP already parallelizes, the model fuses two loops — better than DiscoPoP alone.

s211_distributed_dp_annotates_exposed_lo.shows: Pre-flight (e1_smoke5): the restructuring path end to end — the model distributes the loop, DiscoPoP annotates the exposed parallel half, TSan rejects the racy one.

s321_recurrence_declined_9_attempts.shows: Pre-flight (e1_smoke5): a recurrence declined after 9 attempts, every one rejected by the gate.

floyd_restructured_peeling.shows: With the speed check on: a restructuring of floyd-warshall kept at 9.6× (12 threads); DiscoPoP alone reaches nothing.

floyd_stack_array_broken.shows: E10's one unsafe result: a stack array sized by the problem — correct at the dump size, it crashes at the verification size with 6 threads. The contract now states the memory limit.

hotspot_correct_but_12x_slower.shows: Speed check off: a correct parallel hotspot that is not faster (0.97×/0.95×) — the kind of change the speed check exists to keep out.

lu_inner_pragma_correct_but_5x_slower.shows: Speed check off: correct pragmas on lu's inner loop, 5× slower (0.21×/0.16×).

lu_with_speed_check_faster.shows: Speed check on, at the timing size: one pragma kept on lu, 2.4× at 12 threads.

lu_annotated_after_fix84.shows: After Fix 84: pragmas on lu, 2.72× where DiscoPoP alone gives 0.21×.

2mm_annotated_faster.shows: Pragmas only on 2mm, 7.5× at 12 threads; DiscoPoP alone was timed on another setup, so no ratio.

seidel2d_correctly_declined.shows: A true recurrence declined: 12 attempts, 8 rejected for wrong output and 4 for races.

floyd_restructured_faster.shows: Pilot 4: the first kept restructuring of floyd-warshall, 2.9× at 12 threads.

jacobi2d_annotated_faster.shows: Pilot 4: pragmas only on jacobi-2d, 5.8× at 12 threads.

trisolv_reduction_extracted.shows: Pilot 4: the model extracts a reduction in trisolv; the kernel cannot be timed at any size, so correctness only.

bare_s211_r1_distribution_reads_old_b_br.shows: The model alone splits s211 into two parallel loops in the wrong order: a[i] now reads the OLD b[i-1] — wrong at any thread count, shipped because nothing checks it.

bare_s211_r2_distribution_reads_old_b_br.shows: The same wrong distribution of s211 in a second repeat (same code, other comments): the error is systematic, not a draw.

bare_s211_r3_distribution_reads_old_b_br.shows: The same wrong distribution of s211 in a third repeat.

bare_s211_r4_distribution_war_race_broke.shows: s211 distributed in the right order, but the loop b[i] = b[i+1] - … is still parallel over a WAR dependence: a race the output catches.

bare_s211_r5_distribution_war_race_broke.shows: The same racy distribution of s211 in a second repeat — all five s211 trials of the model alone are wrong.

bare_s212_r5_distribution_reads_new_a_br.shows: s212 distributed so that b[i] += a[i+1]*d[i] reads a[i+1] AFTER it was multiplied — the original read it before.

bare_s241_r2_distribution_reads_new_a_br.shows: s241 distributed so that b[i] = a[i]*a[i+1]*d[i] reads the NEW a[i+1] where the original read the old one.

bare_s243_r3_distribution_reads_new_a_br.shows: s243 split into three parallel loops; the third reads a[i+1] already overwritten by the first.

bare_s244_r4_distribution_wrong_order_br.shows: s244 distributed in an order that lets the dead store a[i+1] = … survive where the original overwrites it.
